justification: I am deploying the Gradient Boosting, which scored a test-set MAE of $1.80, RMSE of $3.72 and R² of 0.830. It had the lowest test RMSE of all four models; the next best (Random Forest) reached $3.85. Its test RMSE is 16% higher than its training RMSE ($3.22), so the decision rests on unseen-data performance rather than a memorised fit. Scoring 1,000 trips takes about 7 ms, which is fast enough for a real-time Flask endpoint. Tree ensembles are harder to interpret than a linear model, but feature importances still show which inputs drive the fare.
